comparison: Perfect alignment on claims C1, C2, C68 regarding phage persistence as a phenotypic (not genetic) phenomenon. Both evaluations find the evidence compelling and well-supported by experimental data showing bi-phasic killing curves and proper controls.

Strong agreement on claims C3, C4, C40 distinguishing phage persistence from antibiotic persistence mechanisms. Both accept the negative result as valid. OpenEval notes sample size concerns not mentioned by peer reviewers.

Both support claims C5-C8 on heat-induced phage tolerance. Peer review R3 also covers C9-C12 (tolerance vs resistance distinction and evolutionary implications) which OpenEval addresses separately in R4 and R5. Both find the experimental approaches compelling.

OpenEval R4 addresses claims C9, C10 on tolerance vs resistance distinction. Peer R3 covers these claims along with broader heat tolerance findings (C5-C12). Both evaluations support the distinction between tolerance and resistance phenotypes.

OpenEval R5 focuses on claims C11, C12 regarding tolerance-resistance evolutionary link. Peer R3 includes these claims in broader assessment of heat-induced effects. Both affirm the mechanistic connection between tolerance and resistance evolution.

Both address generalizability claims C13, C14. Peer R4 also covers combination therapy claims C15, C65-C67 (addressed by OpenEval R7). Both strongly support the generalizability across multiple phage-bacteria combinations and clinical strains.

OpenEval R7 focuses on claims C15, C65-C67 regarding combination therapy effectiveness. Peer R4 covers these alongside generalizability claims. Both affirm that heat treatment undermines phage combination therapy with important clinical implications.

Both address mechanistic claims about DNA injection inhibition (C16-C18). Peer R5 covers broader envelope mechanism including C19-C23, C69 (proteomic and LPS findings addressed by OpenEval R9-R10). Both strongly support the mechanistic findings.

OpenEval R9 addresses proteomic findings C19, C69. Peer R5 includes these in comprehensive mechanistic assessment covering C16-C23, C69. Both support the envelope protein reduction findings, though OpenEval notes the mechanistic link is somewhat inferential.

OpenEval R10 covers LPS reduction and polymyxin cross-tolerance claims C20-C23, C70. Peer R5 includes these in broader mechanistic evaluation. Both support the findings, with OpenEval noting clinical implications require further investigation.

Strong agreement on evolutionary findings C24-C29 regarding heat-tolerant mutants. Peer R6 also includes C30 (gain-of-function mutation, addressed by OpenEval R12). Both affirm the experimental evolution design and PspA mutation findings.

OpenEval R12 focuses on claim C30 regarding gain-of-function vs loss-of-function mutations. Peer R6 includes this in broader evolutionary assessment. Both support the genetic analysis, with OpenEval noting molecular mechanism needs further characterization.

Both address capsule reduction claims C32-C34. Peer R7 covers broader phenotypic characterization including C35-C39 (addressed by OpenEval R14-R15). Both support the novel mechanistic link between PspA function and capsule biosynthesis.

OpenEval R14 addresses immune evasion claims C35, C36, C62. Peer R7 includes these in comprehensive mutant characterization. Both support findings, with OpenEval noting modest sample sizes (n=3) for animal studies not mentioned by peer reviewers.

OpenEval R15 covers antibiotic tolerance claims C37-C39. Peer R7 includes these in broader mutant phenotype assessment. Both clearly support the distinction between tolerance and resistance, and the role of PspA in envelope homeostasis.

Both address broader implications including tolerance-resistance parallels (C41, C63). Peer R8 covers wider set of implications claims. Both support the parallel between antibiotic and phage systems, with peer review noting missing relevant citations.

OpenEval R17 addresses trade-off claims C53, C54. Peer R8 includes these in broader implications discussion. Both clearly support the demonstrated trade-offs between phage resistance and immune evasion.

OpenEval R18 addresses fever-related claims C55-C57 with UNCERTAIN evaluation, noting temperatures used (42-50°C) exceed physiological fever (38-40°C). Peer R8 supports broader implications without specifically questioning fever extrapolation. Key disagreement on physiological relevance.

OpenEval R19 addresses mechanistic background claims C43-C46 on heat stress and protein folding. Peer R9 covers broader set of background claims. Both support these as appropriate contextual knowledge, with OpenEval noting direct protein misfolding evidence not provided.

OpenEval R20 addresses PspA background claims C31, C48, C49. Peer R10 covers methodological and system characterization claims including C31, C58, C59, C64. Both accept these as established background knowledge.

OpenEval R21 addresses background claims C50-C52, C59-C61 on established scientific knowledge. Peer R9 covers overlapping and additional background claims. Both support these as appropriate citations providing essential context.

OpenEval R22 addresses background claims C58, C64, C71-C76. Peer R9 covers overlapping background claims. Both accept these as established knowledge with appropriate citations, with peer review noting some relevant previous work missing from discussion.

OpenEval R23 addresses recent literature context claims C42, C47. Peer R9 includes C47 in broader background assessment. Both support these as appropriate prior work citations providing important context.
